# Extras commands

> All `brp extras *` subcommands self-gate on `rpc.discover`: on an app running core BRP only (no `bevy_copilot_extras` plugin) they fail with an informative error naming the plugin; everything else keeps working.

## brp extras screenshot

Capture a screenshot of the Bevy app's primary window

```text
Capture a screenshot of the Bevy app's primary window

Usage: bevy_copilot brp extras screenshot [OPTIONS] --path <PATH>

Options:
      --host <HOST>        Host of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_HOST, default 127.0.0.1)
      --path <PATH>        Destination path for the screenshot
      --camera <CAMERA>    Camera entity ID whose viewport to capture
      --port <PORT>        Port of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_PORT, default 15702)
      --compact <COMPACT>  Compact (single-line) JSON output instead of pretty: true|false [possible values: true, false]
      --entity <ENTITY>    Entity ID to crop the capture to (as seen by --camera)
      --padding <PADDING>  Physical pixels of padding around the entity crop (requires --entity)
  -h, --help               Print help
```

MCP peer: `brp_extras_screenshot`

## brp extras record

Record the Bevy app's primary window as a PNG frame sequence

```text
Record the Bevy app's primary window as a PNG frame sequence

Usage: bevy_copilot brp extras record [OPTIONS] --path <PATH>

Options:
      --host <HOST>        Host of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_HOST, default 127.0.0.1)
      --path <PATH>        Output directory for the recorded frame_%06d.png sequence
      --port <PORT>        Port of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_PORT, default 15702)
      --seconds <SECONDS>  Recording duration in seconds (default: 10)
      --compact <COMPACT>  Compact (single-line) JSON output instead of pretty: true|false [possible values: true, false]
      --fps <FPS>          Capture cadence in frames per second (default: 30)
      --camera <CAMERA>    Camera entity ID whose viewport to record (default: primary window)
      --video <VIDEO>      Also stitch the frames into this MP4 file with ffmpeg when it is on PATH (client-side only; never sent over the wire, never fails the call)
  -h, --help               Print help
```

MCP peer: `brp_extras_record`
